_comment: Hand-maintained mapping from xAI's public pricing page to pricing.json entries.
The page embeds xAI's whole public catalogue as data, in a script that sets
globalThis.__XAI_PUBLIC_MODELS__: per cluster, every language model with its
prices, its aliases and its long-context threshold, and every audio model with
its own. The server-side tools are priced in a table on the same page. Nothing
here is a model list: what the page states is what is published.
Token prices arrive in US cents per 100 million tokens, as xAI's API reference
states for the same fields (GET /v1/language-models): 20000 is $2.00 per million.
Audio prices arrive in units of 1e-10 dollars: perAudioSecond 277778 is the
$0.10 per hour the page shows beside it, perCharacter 150000 the $15.00 per
million characters. Both checked against the page's own table on 2026-11-09.
Prices differ by cluster: on 2026-11-09 us-central-1 charged 10% more for
grok-4.6 and grok-4.7. One cluster is published, the one every language model
is listed in; the others are not published, and the run does not note them every
week. scripts/providers/xai/README.md says so for whoever reads the figures.
Not published yet, though the page states them: image and video generation
(per image, per second of video) and the real-time voice models (per audio token,
per minute of phone line), whose units this file does not represent.
Batch rates are derived from the page's "Batch discounts by model" table, which
applies to every token type, and each entry says so in batch_derived. Not from the
catalogue's batchDiscountPercent: on 2026-11-09 it gave grok-build-0.1 20% while the
table left it out, and states that models not listed have no batch discount.
_comment_audio: Audio models published, and how. A model the page lists that is not named here is
skipped without a note when it is in `audio_skipped`, and noted otherwise.
_comment_tools: The unit words the tool table uses, and the price field each becomes. A price the
table states in any other way ("Token-based", "Imagine API rates") is not a
per-call price, and the tool is left out with a note.
